extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent attorneys, and IP practitioners preparing or prosecuting AI-related patent applications in China
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for drafting, disclosing, and prosecuting patent applications for artificial intelligence-related inventions before CNIPA, covering types of AI applications, inventorship, subject-matter eligibility, disclosure requirements, inventive step examination, and ethics/compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of AI-related patent applications
rubrics_metrics.description: The Guidelines state that there are 4 types of AI-related patent applications: AI algorithms of models themselves; applications of AI algorithms or models in different domains; inventions made with the assistance of AI; and AI-generated inventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this taxonomy to determine filing strategy, disclosure depth, inventorship issues, and which examination rules apply (e.g., whether the inventive contribution is in the model, its training, its application, or machine-generated).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventorship must be a natural person
rubrics_metrics.description: “The inventor should be an individual, and the name of the organization or collective, as well as the name of the artificial intelligence, should not be included in the request”. The inventor whose name appears in the patent document must be a natural person; non-natural persons (including AI systems) may not be inventors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For inventions made with the assistance of AI, name as inventor a natural person who has made a creative contribution to the substantive features of the invention. For inventions generated by AI, current Chinese legal context does not permit granting inventor status to AI. Rights tied to inventorship (income, signature) are civil rights and can only be held by civil subjects (natural or legal persons).

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract mathematical algorithms (no technical features) are not patentable
rubrics_metrics.description: If the claims of a patent application involving artificial intelligence algorithms or models only involve abstract mathematical theories or mathematical algorithms and do not contain any technical features, they are rules and methods of intellectual activities and cannot be granted patent rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of unpatentable subject matter include a method for establishing a general neural network model based only on abstract algorithmic description, or training a general neural network using an optimized loss function without any technical features. Claims should avoid being framed solely as abstract math/algorithmic rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scenario 1 — technical solution when AI processes data with precise technical meaning
rubrics_metrics.description: A solution is a technical solution if the claim reflects that the object processed by the AI algorithm/model is data with a precise technical meaning in the technical field, and a person skilled in the art can see that executing the algorithm embodies use of laws of nature to solve a technical problem and obtains a technical effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Draft claims to tie input/output data to precise technical meanings and show how processing those data solves a technical problem (e.g., image recognition/classification). Show how steps of processing features are closely related to the technical problem and produce a corresponding technical effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scenario 2 — technical solution when there is a specific technical connection between algorithm/model and internal computer structure
rubrics_metrics.description: If the claim reflects a specific technical connection between the AI algorithm/model and the internal structure of the computer system that solves technical problems such as improving hardware computing efficiency, reducing storage/transmission, or improving processing speed, and obtains technical effects of improving internal performance of the computer system, the solution is a technical solution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific technical association may be shown by adapting algorithms to hardware parameters (e.g., adjusting pruning granularity to memristor array size), optimizing system resource configuration, changing system architecture or parameters, or algorithmic adaptations constrained by hardware conditions. The Guidelines note that the hardware structure need not be physically changed; optimization of resource scheduling can suffice. Conversely, a negative example: claims that merely recite a conventional memory and processor storing instructions to run a neural-network training method (with no specific technical connection) do not constitute a technical solution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scenario 3 — technical solution when mining intrinsic correlations that conform to natural laws in specific application fields
rubrics_metrics.description: When AI algorithms/models are used to mine intrinsic correlations in big data in a specific application field and those correlations conform to natural laws, thereby solving technical problems (e.g., improving reliability/accuracy of analysis) and producing technical effects, the claim constitutes a technical scheme.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarify in the claim/specification which indicators, parameters, etc. reflect the characteristics of the analyzed object and whether the intrinsic correlations between these inputs and model outputs conform to natural laws. Use examples (food safety knowledge graph with timestamps reflecting changing food properties) to show how the correlations follow natural law. By contrast, correlations governed only by economic or social laws (e.g., predicting an economic prosperity index) do not constitute use of natural laws and are not technical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequate disclosure / sufficiency of description for AI inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: The specification should clearly record the technical solution, describe in detail specific implementation methods, and fully disclose the technical content essential for understanding and realizing the invention so that a technician in the relevant field can implement it. AI 'black box' characteristics require sufficient information to achieve full disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record and fully describe the parts that contribute over prior art. State beneficial effects objectively and provide evidence when necessary. Recommended practices by invention-type: for model training contributions, disclose the algorithms, specific steps, and training process; for model construction, disclose module structure, hierarchy, connections, functions, and demonstrated effects (experimental data if necessary); for applications in specific fields, clarify how the model combines with the scenario, how input/output data are set, and correlations between inputs and outputs. When issuing a disclosure insufficiency opinion, explain the reasons based on the original description and claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventiveness examination — when algorithmic features count toward inventive step
rubrics_metrics.description: To include algorithmic features as part of the technical means in the inventiveness assessment, claims should show that the AI algorithms/models are applied to specific functions or application fields and solve specific technical problems so that algorithmic features and technical features functionally support each other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the algorithm/model in the application is prior art, consider the distance between technical fields, whether there is technical inspiration to apply it, difficulty of applying across fields, necessity to overcome technical difficulties, and whether unexpected technical effects arise. If application to a new field only changes the meaning of data (e.g., counting ships versus fruits) without changing processing methods, model training, or producing unexpected technical effects, the application is likely predictable and lacks inventiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventive step when algorithm features combine with hardware or user-experience improvements
rubrics_metrics.description: If the AI algorithm/model has a specific technical relationship with internal computer structure and improves internal performance, or if algorithm features and technical features jointly improve user experience, consider the algorithmic and technical features as a whole when judging inventiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: (1) an algorithm adjusted to run on a low-bit FPGA that, together with low-bit hardware parameters, solves resource constraints and improves internal performance — considered inventive when prior art lacks such technical inspiration; (2) an AI-driven automatic switching system for chatbot/manual service that analyzes load and reallocates requests to reduce wait time and improve user experience — considered inventive if prior art did not provide technical inspiration for automatic switching based on AI analysis. When the combination yields unexpected technical effects and prior art gives no inspiration, the combined solution can be inventive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics, data compliance, and public-interest considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent applications on AI-related content should comply with Article 5 of China’s Patent Law. Applicants should consider whether algorithms/models violate laws/regulations, social morality, or are detrimental to the public interest when applied to specific scenarios. Data acquisition and utilization must follow relevant laws and regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pay attention not only to the content of the data but also to collection, storage, processing, and safety management practices. Ensure data sources, application scenarios, security, and norms comply with legal and ethical requirements; applications that violate social morality or public interest may be problematic for patentability or prosecution.
